dedupe_keys.name: virtual damage assessment and first floor elevation estimation application to fort myers beach florida and hurricane ian 2022

description: Virtual Damage Assessment and First-floor Elevation Estimation: Application to Fort Myers Beach, Florida and Hurricane Ian (2022) is a dataset listed in DesignSafe Data Depot (published projects), a research data repository for natural hazards engineering under the section "field recon", published or maintained by Mehrshad Amini, University of Rhode Island (uri.edu). Several field work and reconnaissance data -primarily pre- and post-storm street-level and aerial imagery- were used to create a collection of datasets for virtual damage assessment (VDA) and first-floor elevation (FFE) measurements of 3,408 building structures impacted by Hurricane Ian (2022) in Fort Myers Beach, Florida. Coverage: Fort Myers Beach, FL. DesignSafe files it as a "field recon" project. Keywords: Hurricane Ian, Damage assessment , Structural damage, First-floor elevation, Coastal buildings . Published 2024-12-31. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is ODC-By-1.0. Caveats: this record was written from the catalogue listing only, so the linked page was not opened, its contents and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support structural performance, hazard exposure and resilience studies. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-designsafe-data-depot-repository.
